subject: Re: PayGrid model fit / eval follow-up — recommended models & parity thresholds

Subject: PayGrid — follow-up on model fit / parity discussion

Thanks for the call today, Marissa.

Quick recap and asks from our side:
- We're happy with the latency/cost profile you showed for Redwood Dedicated, but what matters most is accuracy on our downstream tasks (payment intent extraction, payer name normalization, and fraud flagging).
- Today we use an internal parser (proprietary LSTM/CRF pipeline) and baseline metrics are: intent extraction F1=0.88, name normalization accuracy=0.92, fraud-flag recall=0.90.

Can you share:
1) Recommended open models for an apples-to-apples eval against our baseline (we'd like to run a blind A/B).
2) A suggested acceptance threshold for parity (how close is "good enough").
3) Any example prompt sets and the benchmark harness you suggest we run.

If you can attach the prompt set and a short eval doc that would help us kick off next week. Thanks — Samir

--
Samir Khan
Director of ML, PayGrid

Subject: Re: PayGrid — follow-up on model fit / parity discussion

Samir — great to connect yesterday, and thanks for the clear baseline numbers. Short answers below and attached is a starter prompt set (paygrid_prompt_set_v2.jsonl) plus a short eval playbook (paygrid_eval_report_20260304.pdf).

1) Recommended open models (to run in your dev eval):
   - Redwood-Open-XL-13B (8-bit): good balance of instruction-following and structured extraction.
   - Mistral-Instruct-7B (q4_0): very cost-effective, often matches XL on extraction tasks after prompt tuning.
   - Llama2-13B-Instruct (preferred 8-bit quantized variant): good for name normalization with minimal hallucination.

2) Acceptance thresholds (suggested parity criteria):
   - Intent extraction F1 >= 0.90 relative to human labels OR within 0.03 absolute of your baseline (so >= 0.85 if your baseline shifts).
   - Name normalization accuracy >= 0.91 (within 1% of baseline).
   - Fraud-flag recall >= 0.88 while keeping false positive rate <= +2% vs baseline.
   - Operational: median generation latency <= 400ms at 95th percentile for 1-2 token responses (your real distribution might be higher; we'll include config suggestions).

3) Prompt sets / harness: attached paygrid_prompt_set_v2.jsonl contains: positive/negative examples, canonical outputs (for automated scoring), and edge-case prompts. We recommend running the harness in our evaluation notebook (link in the PDF) which outputs F1/accuracy/recall and confidence-calibrated thresholds.

Next steps: please confirm you want us to spin up a short Dedicated eval pool (2x A100-equivalent) and we'll run the models and return a concise report (2–3 days). If you prefer to run in-house, we can provide the harness and suggested config.

I copied Aditya and Dev for technical follow-up on quantization/config and evaluation infra.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi all — adding a few technical notes to help interpret results and avoid regression traps.

- Model variants: for each candidate model, run both the instruction-tuned and the "few-shot" prompt formats. Some extraction tasks benefit from 1–3 shot examples.
- Quantization: run 8-bit (or q4) variants first. For the 13B models we recommend 8-bit LLM quantization with KV-cache preserved. We'll share the exact kernel flags in the notebook.
- Evaluation metrics: use micro-averaged F1 for slot-style extraction, exact-match for canonicalization (name normalization), and recall at fixed precision for fraud flagging.
- Acceptance and regression: be conservative about small improvements that come with greater hallucination. If accuracy improves but hallucination increases, that can be worse in prod. We flag any absolute drop > 0.02 in name accuracy or > 0.03 in intent F1 as a regression that needs a manual review.

I'll attach a short script (in the Drive link) that converts your golden-label CSV to the eval harness format. Happy to run the first pass if you share a sample.

—Aditya (ML Eng)

Marissa / Aditya — thanks, this is helpful. A couple of clarifying Qs from our data team:
1) For fraud-flag recall, we're sensitive to any drop because we have regulatory SLA obligations. Is there a way to run a canary where the model suggestions are scored but not actioned until we pass a threshold?
2) On name normalization, can you share an example failure case you typically see with open models?

We can share a sanitized sample of 2k labeled rows by tomorrow. Please confirm whether you can run the Dedicated eval (preferred) and estimated cost/time.

Thanks — Priya
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@paygrid.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@paygrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: PayGrid — follow-up on model fit / parity discussion

Priya — great questions. Quick answers and proposed plan: 

1) Canary flow: yes — recommend a scoring-only canary for 7 days where Redwood returns model scores + recommended canonical outputs but your pipeline only logs them (no downstream action). After the canary you can compare distributional drift and measure recall/precision without risk. We'll set up automatic alerting if model recall drops below the threshold you define.

2) Typical name-normalization failure modes:
   - Rare international name ordering (e.g., no clear delimiter between family/given), leading to swapped fields.
   - OCR/noisy inputs where punctuation is missing — models sometimes invent extra tokens instead of normalizing.
   - Ambiguous honorifics or concatenated tokens ("DrJohn" -> "Dr John") requiring lightweight rule post-processing.

Estimated eval plan & cost: spin up a 48-hour Dedicated eval (2x A100-equivalent) for the three candidate models, run on your 2k sample with our harness, and deliver a report + suggested config (batching, quantization flags). Estimated cost: ~$2.7k for the Dedicated run (standalone evaluation); turnaround 48–72 hours depending on queue. If you'd like us to run the first pass, please share the sanitized sample and an NDA if needed (we can accept hashed PII).

Proposed next step: Samir/Priya — share the sample and confirm you want Redwood to run the Dedicated eval. We'll post a short SOW and timeline.

—Marissa
